title: One-time Wage Adjustment for Civil Servants to Offset Anticipated High Core Inflation Rate in 2022
what_it_is: One-time Wage Adjustment for Civil Servants to Offset Anticipated High Core Inflation Rate in 2022

sections.label: Civil servant salary adjustments and support
sections.summary: Recent civil servant salary adjustments were based on market benchmarks, with AVC payments and increments exceeding inflation, plus support measures for households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The recent salary adjustments for various groups of civil servants were determined based on salary gaps with market benchmarks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Beyond these adjustments, eligible officers also receive Annual Variable Component (AVC) payments and annual salary increments that take into consideration their performance, prevailing economic and labour market conditions and the National Wages Council’s recommendations on progressive wage growth.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In total, the salary increases arising from the recent salary reviews and annual salary increments, coupled with annual AVC payments, will more than exceed the inflation rate seen this year for all the civil servants who meet the criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Government has also rolled out a series of support measures this year, such as the recently announced Cost-of-Living Special Payment and additional CDC Vouchers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: These support measures together will help to cushion the impact of sharp inflation changes and provide further relief for Singaporean households, with more support for lower- to middle-income groups.

sections.label: Spillover to companies and NWC recommendations
sections.summary: The Government asks whether its increment above inflation encourages companies to follow, and notes MOM and NWC recommendations for the wider economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The second supplementary question is: if that is so, that the Government is keeping the increment to more than 5.1% or inflation rate, would it encourage the rest of the Singapore companies to do the same as far as possible?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: There might be a very, very small number of people who do not meet the performance criteria and they might be short of that 5% that the Member mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On top of that, the Government has all the other packages for all the Singaporean households, which we think will be able to meet the requirement to help those who are most in need.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: On the second supplementary question, MOM together with the National Wages Council (NWC) has laid out its own recommendations for the rest of the economy to do what we can and especially do more, if possible, for those households and individuals who need more help.
